messages.subject: scales library

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: scales library
parts:
It's been a while, but this used to happen and then Hadley went away from it because most of the time you don't need the scales package so you would be unnecessarily loading it. There were other packages loaded previously  too and those are no longer loaded as well. 

Does your suggestion make sense? Yes, because many people have struggled with this, but also no because loading things unnecessarily is wasteful and can cause collision with other loaded things. 

I suppose it was Hadley's choice to make.

B

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: scales library
parts:
Sean, 

Not that I can see. If you need to scale or transform your axes then you probably need it, if not, you probably don't. I don't believe you should be able to tell by the use of certain geom_*'s in ggplot2 that you need to load scales. 

If you're sick of guessing, put it in your Rprofile. See here for an example:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/10300769/how-to-load-packages-in-r-automatically

I will echo the comments of some on doing this though, in that it's generally a bad idea if you expect your code to be portable. 

HTH, 

Brandon
